question.text: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, determine the value of $x$ that satisfies the equation $e^{2x-1}= 3 \cdot 8^{x}.$
question.explanation:
First, we take the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation:

\begin{align*} e^{2x-1} &= 3 \cdot 8^{x} \\[3pt] \ln \left(e^{2x-1}\right) & = \ln \left(3 \cdot 8^{x}\right) \end{align*}

Now, we use the fact that $\ln \left( e^a \right) = a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

\[ 2x - 1 = \ln \left( 3 \cdot 8^x\right) . \]

Next, we use the power and product laws of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

\begin{align*} 2x - 1 &= \ln (3) + \ln (8^x) \\[3pt] 2x - 1 &= \ln (3) + x\ln (8) \\[3pt] \end{align*}

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

\begin{align*} 2x - 1 & = \ln (3) +x\ln(8)\\[5pt] 2x & =\ln (3) + x\ln(8) +1 \\[5pt] 2x - x\ln(8) &= \ln (3) + 1\\[5pt] x (2 - \ln(8)) & = \ln (3) + 1 \\[5pt] x & = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ \dfrac{\ln (3) + 1}{2 - \ln(8)} } \end{align*}

question.text: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, determine the value of $x$ that satisfies the equation $e^{2x-2} = 2 \cdot 9^{x}.$
question.explanation:
First, we take the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation:

\begin{align*} e^{2x-2} &= 2 \cdot 9^{x} \\[3pt] \ln \left(e^{2x-2}\right) & = \ln \left( 2 \cdot 9^{x}\right) \end{align*}

Now, we use the fact that $\ln \left( e^a \right) = a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

\[ 2x - 2 = \ln \left( 2 \cdot 9 ^x\right). \]

Next, we use the power and product laws of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

\begin{align*} 2x - 2 &= \ln (2)+ \ln (9^x)\\[3pt] 2x - 2 &= \ln (2)+ x\ln (9) \end{align*}

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

\begin{align*} 2x - 2 & = \ln (2)+x\ln(9)\\[5pt] 2x - x\ln(9) &= 2+\ln (2)\\[5pt] x (2 - \ln(9)) & = 2+\ln (2) \\[5pt] x & = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ \dfrac{ 2+\ln (2)}{2 - \ln(9)} } \end{align*}

question.text: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, determine the value of $x$ that satisfies the equation $e^{4x}=4^{1-x}.$
question.explanation:
First, we take the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation:

\begin{align*} e^{4x} &=4^{1-x} \\[3pt] \ln \left(e^{4x}\right) & = \ln \left(4^{1-x}\right) \end{align*}

Now, we use the fact that $\ln \left( e^a \right) = a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

\[ 4x = \ln \left( 4^{1-x}\right). \]

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

\[ 4x = ( 1-x )\ln (4) \]

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

\begin{align*} 4x & = ( 1-x )\ln(4)\\[5pt] 4x & = \ln(4) - x\ln(4)\\[5pt] 4x + x\ln(4) &= \ln(4) \\[5pt] x (4 + \ln(4)) & = \ln(4) \\[5pt] x & = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ \dfrac{\ln(4)}{4 + \ln(4)} } \end{align*}

question.text: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, determine the value of $x$ that satisfies the equation $7^{3x}=9^{6-x}.$
question.explanation:
First, we take the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation: \begin{align*} 7^{3x}&=9^{6-x} \\[5pt] \ln\left(7^{3x}\right) & = \ln\left(9^{6-x}\right) \end{align*}

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives \[ 3x\ln(7) = (6-x)\ln(9). \]

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows: \begin{align*} 3x\ln(7) & = (6-x)\ln(9)\\[5pt] 3x\ln(7) & = 6\ln(9)-x\ln(9) \\[5pt] 3x\ln(7) +x\ln(9) & = 6\ln(9) \\[5pt] x\left(3\ln(7)+\ln(9)\right) & = 6\ln(9) \\[5pt] x & = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{6\ln(9)}{3\ln(7)+\ln(9)}} \end{align*}

question.explanation:
First, we take the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation:

\begin{align*} 4^{7x+3} & =10^{x+8} \\[3pt] \ln\left(4^{7x+3}\right) & = \ln\left(10^{x+8}\right) \end{align*}

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

\begin{align*} (7x+3)\ln(4) & = (x+8)\ln(10) \end{align*}

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

\begin{align*} (7x+3)\ln(4) & = (x+8)\ln(10) \\[5pt] 7x\ln(4)+3\ln(4) & = x\ln(10)+8\ln(10) \\[5pt] 7x\ln(4)-x\ln(10) & = 8\ln(10)-3\ln(4) \\[5pt] x\left(7\ln(4)-\ln(10)\right) & = 8\ln(10)-3\ln(4) \\[5pt] x & = \dfrac{8\ln(10)-3\ln(4)}{7\ln(4)-\ln(10)} \end{align*}
